MINUTES
  GENERAL PLAN ADVISORY COMMITTEE MEETING
  MAY 15, 2018
A regular meeting of the General Plan Advisory Committee (GPAC) of the City of Rolling Hills
Estates was called to order at 6:10 p.m. in the City Hall Council Chambers, 4045 Palos Verdes
Drive North, by CHAIR ZUCKERMAN.

2.  ROLL CALL

  Committee Members Present:  Chair Zuckerman, Schmitz, Medawar, Addleman,
  Arata, Bayer, Buresh, Carrese, Corman, Friedman,
  Portugal, Seamans, Shinn, Silvano, Stegura,
  Wagreich

  Committee Members Absent:  Carman

  Staff Present:  Planning Director Wahba, Assistant City Manager
  Grammer, Sr. Planner Naughton, Administrative
  Assistant Corea

  Also present from Dyett & Bhatia:  Rajeev Bhatia, Elizabeth Blanton, Meghan McNulty

3.  APPROVAL OF MINUTES

  A.  APPROVAL OF GENERAL PLAN ADVISORY COMMITTEE DRAFT MINUTES,
  MEETING OF FEBRUARY 6, 2018

  A MOTION WAS MADE TO APPROVE THE MINUTES OF THE GPAC MEETING
  OF FEBRUARY 6, 2018, AS PRESENTED.

  There being no objection, CHAIR ZUCKERMAN so ordered.

4.  AUDIENCE ITEMS WRITTEN/ORAL COMMUNICATIONS NOT ON THE AGENDA

  None

5.  DISCUSSION ITEMS

  A.  PROCESS UPDATE (DYETT & BHATIA)

  - Project status

  Rajeev Bhatia, Dyett & Bhatia, provided the committee with status on the task list and
  stated that this meeting will focus on ideas for the future. Mr. Bhatia provided a brief
  overview of the tasks that the committee (with support from his team) will be working on
  after this meeting, which include: developing a preferred plan/strategy for any specific
  land use changes and transportation improvements; writing of the General Plan policies;
  and an Environmental Impact Report (EIR).

  1
GPAC Meeting Minutes
May 15, 2018
   - Review of what we heard at GPAC Meeting #2

  Mr. Bhatia provided a brief summary of the topics which were discussed at the last meeting.

  B.  RESULTS OF COMMUNITY OUTREACH/DRAFT VISION AND GUIDING
  PRINCIPLES (DYETT & BHATIA)

  - Results of online survey and Earth Day pop-up event

  Meghan McNulty stated that the results of the Community Stakeholder Interviews, the
  online survey, and the Earth Day pop-up event may be found on the General Plan Update
  (GPU) web page, in the Library section (https://rhegeneralplan.org/library/).

  Ms. McNulty provided a PowerPoint presentation with a summary of the results of the
  survey and outreach events.

  In response to a question by CHAIR ZUCKERMAN, Ms. McNulty stated that a list of those
  who participated in the community stakeholders interviews can be found in Appendix A of
  the Stakeholder Interviews Report found on the GPU web page.

  In response to a question by CHAIR ZUCKERMAN, Elizabeth Blanton, Dyett & Bhatia
  stated that the city received a 2% response rate from the survey, which is good. Mr. Bahtia
  stated that there will be continuing outreach which will correspond with where the project
  is at the time.

  In response to a question by COMMITTEE MEMBER STEGURA regarding online survey
  question 4, 47% of respondents age 45 and older said that the city should expand its
  equestrian facilities. She asked it was representative of the number of horse owners and
  also asked if the survey received a disproportionate amount of responses from
  equestrians. Mr. Bhatia stated that the survey was self-selected and to keep in mind that
  those who take survey usually have something specific that they would like to relay.

  A discussion ensued regarding specifics of the survey, including the percentage of
  respondents, the wording of the survey questions, and answers to the survey questions.

  In response to the question of any surprising results from the survey, the committee
  members commented that the survey responses were consistent with discussions during
  previous GPAC meetings, the responses for preserving environmental resources
  compared to adding more retail, and that people would like to see housing on Silver Spur
  Road.

  A comment was made that the question regarding equestrians was phrased incorrectly.
  People want to preserve what is already existing, but not necessarily expand equestrian
  facilities. In addition, categories grouped together such as restaurants/bars and
  hotels/office should have been broken up individually to get a better idea of what people
  really want to see in the city.

  - Review and discussion of Community Vision and Guiding Principles

  Ms. Blanton provided a description of what the Community Vision and Guiding Principles
  statements are to achieve and led a discussion on the draft document.

  2
GPAC Meeting Minutes
May 15, 2018
   A discussion ensued and comments included: the lack of mention of youth and family-
  friendly recreation facilities and entertainment, making one of the residential developments
  at Deep Valley Drive 55+ only housing, having a skatepark in the city, providing safer
  walking accommodations, future discussion on traffic conditions and improving retail
  business, and future discussion on a community center.

  Comments were made that adding a community center may not be a good idea since not
  many people would use it, however, ideas were suggested to create a place for people to
  gather, such as an amphitheater, a fountain, or a skatepark. The document should also
  include quality schools and libraries, and that the city is a relaxing and stress-free place.

  Planning Director Wahba provided background on the last General Plan Update and the
  discussions and ideas proposed at that time. He stated that discussion should focus on
  the main commercial district and does not foresee any of the other land use designations
  changing. Planning Director Wahba provided an explanation on the difference between a
  general plan and a specific plan, and current development projects.

  C.  GENERAL PLAN CONCEPTS BRAINSTORM (DYETT & BHATIA)

  No discussion on this item.

6.  COMMITTEE ITEMS/FUTURE AGENDA ITEMS

  The next GPAC meeting will continue the discussion on improvements to the commercial
  district with the recommendation that committee members visit the businesses within the
  commercial district.

  Mr. Bhatia suggested that committee members taking individual tours to the following in
  mind:
  • It is a 1-mile walk from end to end.
  • Think about where the local-serving amenities are and if those should remain.
  • Are you looking for continuity of retail presence on the ground level, and if so,
  where?
  • Scale of development, specifically take a look at the new 4-story project.
  • Land use designations.

7.  ADJOURNMENT

  The meeting adjourned at 8:35 PM.

  __________________________
  Carol Corea  Heidi Luce
  Minutes Secretary  City Clerk

  3
GPAC Meeting Minutes
May 15, 2018
